name: Maya
label: Artist-pay critic, still streaming
who: I think streaming pays artists too little, and I judge services partly on their royalties. I have moved to Apple Music over artist pay and miss Spotify, though I have also kept Spotify out of habit.
value_for_money: They judge value mostly by how artists are paid rather than by features, saying Spotify pays artists fractions of a cent per stream while earning large revenue. Some argue the subscription is cheap relative to what listeners get, but the artist side is what matters to them.
loyalty: They keep using Spotify out of habit and for its features, but royalty rates are the main reason some have left. They say they would move to a service that pays artists more per stream.
pain_points: Royalty deals and label influence on recommendations
likes: Familiar app after years of use
reasons_to_stay: They say ease of discovery and their long habit with the app keep them there. Their main complaint is about royalties rather than features, and they treat the app's usefulness as separate from how artists are paid.
tone: Argumentative and analytical, citing royalty reasoning and business logic, with a sharp and sometimes sarcastic edge.
